hinglish.title: Operating System 02 | CPU Scheduling Algorithms | CS & IT | GATE 2025 Crash Course
hinglish.why: A single ~121-min crash-course lecture by Vishvadeep Gothi (GATE Wallah/PW) that a viewer's own timestamp comment confirms runs through criteria, FCFS, SJF, SRTF, Priority, Aging, Round Robin and finally Multilevel Queue scheduling with Gantt-chart examples for each — by far the most complete single Hinglish video found for this topic (competing channels split the same scope across 9-11 separate uploads). Views (85.7K) are modest next to Gate Smashers' per-algorithm uploads, but comment sentiment is uniformly positive ('concept crystal clear', 'you teach with so much energy') with no reported numerical errors.

hinglish.title: L-2.11: Multilevel Feedback Queue Scheduling | Operating System
covers: Multilevel Feedback Queue scheduling concept and structure
hinglish.why: Added specifically to close the one real gap left by the GATE Wallah crash course (which stops at plain Multilevel Queue scheduling). Gate Smashers is the most-watched Hindi GATE channel for this whole unit (each individual algorithm video sits at 1-4M views); this MLFQ video alone has 895K views, 15K likes and near-universal praise ('Faith in humanity restored', 'One of the rarest channels to clear OS concepts') with no accuracy complaints in the top comments.

english.title: All CPU Scheduling Algorithm in 1 Hour -FCFS | SJF | SRTF | Round Robin | Operating System
english.why: The only English-medium video found that bundles terminology, preemption concepts, and worked Gantt-chart examples for FCFS, SJF, SRTF and Round Robin into one sitting (confirmed via its chapter markers). Every fragmented alternative (Neso Academy, Jenny's Lectures) splits these same four algorithms across 4+ separate uploads. View count (20.6K) is lower than the gold-standard channels, and one viewer questioned a completion-time value in the SJF example (1 like, unresolved) — a minor caveat worth a sanity-check, but the rest of the (small) comment section is entirely positive.
comment_highlights: Very clear mam. Every class I learned the subject in new perspective.

runners_up.title: L-2.1: Process Scheduling Algorithms (Preemption Vs Non-Preemption) | CPU Scheduling in OS
runners_up.reason_rejected: Extremely popular but only ~1/11th of the syllabus scope per video; picking the full Gate Smashers series would need 9-11 videos, well over the 3-video cap.

runners_up.title: L-2.3: First Come First Serve(FCFS) CPU Scheduling Algorithm with Example
runners_up.reason_rejected: Highest-viewed FCFS video found (4.3M) but single-algorithm; a comparable-quality single video (GATE Wallah crash course) covers FCFS plus 6 other subtopics.

runners_up.title: Operating System 02 : CPU Scheduling Algorithms | CS & IT | GATE 2026 Crash Course
runners_up.reason_rejected: Same instructor/format as the chosen sCpdv8H6bnQ (2025 edition) but fewer views/likes and no confirmed chapter breakdown; the 2025 edition was preferred.

runners_up.title: CPU Scheduling Algorithms (FCFS, SJF, Round Robin) | Learn Coding
runners_up.reason_rejected: High views and covers FCFS/SJF/SRTF/RR in one video, but its only available transcript is auto-detected as Hindi ('hi'), suggesting mixed/Hindi delivery despite the English title — too risky to classify as an English pick.

runners_up.title: FCFS(First Come First Serve) CPU Scheduling Algorithm with example | Operating System
runners_up.reason_rejected: Confirmed English audio and very high views, but single-algorithm; including it plus the needed SJF/SRTF/Priority/RR/MLQ/MLFQ videos from Jenny's would exceed the 3-video cap.

runners_up.title: FCFS scheduling Algorithm | Convoy Effect | Process Scheduling | OS
runners_up.reason_rejected: Nicely bundles FCFS + Convoy Effect, but choosing it would have displaced one of the three picks needed for broader (SJF/SRTF/RR/Priority/MLQ/MLFQ) coverage; convoy effect is a smaller-weight subtopic by comparison.

runners_up.title: L-2.10: Multi Level Queue Scheduling | Operating System
runners_up.reason_rejected: Excellent MLQ video, but not needed for the Hinglish picks since the chosen GATE Wallah crash course already ends with a Multilevel Queue Scheduling segment.

runners_up.title: Round Robin Scheduling | CPU Scheduling | Operating System | Target GATE 2024
runners_up.reason_rejected: English-dubbed GATE Wallah content exists but each session has under 3,000 views/comments, far too little audience validation.

coverage_gaps: Hinglish: the GATE Wallah crash course's Multilevel Queue segment is brief (~13 min) and 'convoy effect' as a named term was not independently transcript-verified (only inferred from the 'FCFS advantages/disadvantages' chapter). English: 'convoy effect' as an explicitly named term was not confirmed in any of the three picks (FCFS is taught via Unify Study without a dedicated convoy-effect segment); the Unify Study video's view count (20.6K) is much lower than the other picks so it has thinner community vetting, and one unresolved viewer comment questioned a single SJF completion-time value in that video.
